taxonomy.title: Hernia — inguinal, femoral and postrepair pain
taxonomy.scopeIn: Groin anatomy and imaging, inguinal/femoral repair selection, recurrence, acute irreducibility and postherniorrhaphy pain.
taxonomy.scopeOut: Ventral/incisional hernias belong to hernia-ventral-abdominal-wall. Age-specific childhood groin decisions belong to pediatric-gi-abdominal-wall. General peripheral nerve localization belongs to neuro-orthopedic-essentials.
taxonomy.priorityReason: Common surgery and existing owner-returned variants warrant a full concept-family audit.
researchAgenda: Recurrence plane and nerve injury decisions
Symptom attribution and treatment after prior repair
taxonomy.coverageReason: Live identities cover part of this scope. The research agenda flags breadth to check, and the topic worker must judge redundancy and question quality.
taxonomy.testingWeightBasis: Owner-directed editorial estimate of general-surgery testing relevance. No exam percentages or official blueprint weights are asserted.

release.catalogRegistryMeaning: 610 registered concept identities include 156 with no live node. Active coverage uses the 454 primaryConceptId identities actually scored in default-release nodes.

concepts.displayName: Timely elective repair planning for femoral hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Arrange timely elective repair evaluation for a stable reducible femoral hernia.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Recognize the femoral exception to inguinal watchful waiting
concepts.learningObjective: Use current vascular/ligament landmarks to reclassify a groin sac and apply the repair boundary despite improved function.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Interpret the ultrasound neck compartment and partial bowel-wall perfusion to select hernia type and operative exploration versus manual reduction despite continued intestinal passage.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Attribute a marked groin swelling to the correct ultrasound neck among competing findings, then apply the anatomy-dependent boundary of watchful waiting.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Classify a groin sac by ultrasound compartment
concepts.learningObjective: Classify a groin sac by interpreting its neck relative to the inguinal ligament and vascular landmarks.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Select a dynamic groin acquisition from the recorded anatomical course
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a distal cord finding relative to the inferior epigastric vessels and select the additional acquisition that can trace its proximal origin.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Request a symptom-matched dynamic groin acquisition
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish musculoskeletal and posture-dependent groin observations and choose the targeted ultrasound acquisition rather than a generic modality escalation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Recognize acute painful irreducibility with obstructive features as requiring emergency surgical-capable evaluation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Use the relationship among a direct inguinal defect, Hesselbach's triangle, the inferior epigastric vessels, and the transversalis fascia to classify and locate the defect during open repair.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Dynamic ultrasound after an equivocal inguinal-hernia examination
concepts.learningObjective: Select targeted dynamic groin ultrasound for the scoped stable patient with intermittent symptoms and an equivocal examination.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Resolve occult-groin imaging and symptom discordance
concepts.learningObjective: Choose an adequate targeted repeat study or dynamic cross-sectional assessment by interpreting prior scan localization, provocation, symptom reproduction and competing musculoskeletal findings.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Identify an indirect inguinal hernia by its passage lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels through the deep ring.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve sensory pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Localize isolated anterolateral-thigh sensory symptoms after laparoscopic inguinal repair to the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Choose the operative plane for a symptomatic recurrent inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret the archived operative anatomy and choose an offered posterior repair after prior anterior mesh surgery rather than repeat the operated plane.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Elective referral for symptomatic reducible inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Select elective surgical referral for a stable adult with a symptomatic, readily reducible inguinal hernia and no urgent features.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Watchful waiting for selected inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Offer informed watchful waiting to a man with a reducible asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic inguinal hernia.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Elective planning for symptomatic inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Recommend elective repair discussion and planning after a reducible inguinal hernia is confirmed in a patient with meaningful activity-limiting symptoms.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Apply symptom attribution to a demonstrated inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish hernia-related from coexisting musculoskeletal pain and select a repair discussion or observation without assuming every positive image explains the patient's limitation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Prioritize care when groin findings have competing symptom sources
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate interval functional observations with a demonstrated reducible inguinal hernia and coexisting musculoskeletal findings to choose the current care priority.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Evidence boundary for inguinal-hernia watchful waiting
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the selected adult population for whom watchful waiting with safety-net instructions is guideline-supported.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile dynamic groin anatomy with functional symptoms before choosing a repair or observation plan.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.learningObjective: Reassess a new protrusion-associated component of post-hernia pain before attributing all current symptoms to a previously plausible nerve mechanism.

concepts.learningObjective: Escalate investigation after an adequately targeted negative groin study when recurrent mechanical symptoms and a musculoskeletal alternative remain unresolved.

concepts.learningObjective: Refer a clinically suspected childhood inguinal hernia for pediatric surgical assessment rather than applying adult observation criteria.

decisionNodes.stem: Which focused groin ultrasound acquisition should trace {patientName}’s recorded tissue course proximally?

answerChoices.label: Deep inguinal ring during Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: The lateral-to-epigastric cord course points toward the deep ring. Following the moving tissue proximally there can establish whether it enters through a defect rather than infer the diagnosis from a distal contour or an adductor study.

answerChoices.label: Posterior inguinal wall during Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: This is the nearby direct-hernia region, medial to the epigastric vessels. It does not best follow the lateral cord course actually recorded.

answerChoices.label: Femoral canal during Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: This is another clinically important groin region, below the ligament and medial to the femoral vein; it does not trace the recorded tissue along the inguinal cord.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use the anatomical course to choose the additional focus. The deep ring is lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; the direct region lies medially and the femoral canal follows a different route below the ligament. The recorded distal fat movement is not itself proof of a proximal hernia neck. Follow its origin dynamically rather than infer that the tendon examination settled the contour question. A full study can include all regions and positions; this asks for the added focus, not a universally sufficient protocol.

decisionNodes.stem: Which type of hernia do the ultrasound findings identify in {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia
answerChoices.rationale: The neck lies below the inguinal ligament and medial to the common femoral vein, identifying the femoral-canal route.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Direct inguinal anatomy is defined at Hesselbach's triangle medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. The recorded neck instead follows the below-ligament compartment beside the common femoral vein.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An indirect inguinal sac enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. The reported below-ligament neck and venous relationship identify a different route.

decisionNodes.stem: Which repair should be discussed for {patientName}’s recurrent groin defect?

answerChoices.label: Totally extraperitoneal repair
answerChoices.rationale: The old report describes an anterior mesh plane. A posterior preperitoneal approach is the offered route that avoids re-entering that operated plane for a symptomatic recurrence.

answerChoices.label: Anterior Lichtenstein mesh repair
answerChoices.rationale: This is a valid primary repair, but repeating the anterior mesh approach re-enters the prior operative plane in this recurrence.

answerChoices.label: Anterior Shouldice tissue repair

decisionNodes.explanation: The current functional episode remains consistent with the demonstrated hernia rather than being dismissed because hip disease also exists. This does not establish TEP as superior to every other posterior approach or promise that hernia repair cures the separate hip ache.

clinicalCase.learningSummary: What it is: An inguinal hernia is protrusion of abdominal tissue through the inguinal canal, often noticed as an intermittent groin bulge. Typical presentation: An uncomplicated hernia may enlarge with standing, coughing, lifting, or straining and reduce when supine or with gentle examination. Initial evaluation: Confirm the location and reducibility, characterize symptoms, and look for an acute change, obstruction, skin changes, or systemic illness. Clear cases are often clinical diagnoses. Management in this clinic: Refer a meaningfully symptomatic reducible hernia for elective surgical evaluation. Watchful waiting is a bounded option for selected minimally symptomatic adult men, with explicit return precautions. Red flags requiring urgent care: New irreducibility, escalating pain, vomiting, distension, obstipation, skin changes, peritoneal findings, or systemic illness require emergency evaluation.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should be arranged next for {patientName}'s intermittent groin swelling?

answerChoices.label: Groin ultrasound with standing strain and cine loops
answerChoices.rationale: The outside acquisition documents a different target after the event. A targeted dynamic groin assessment addresses the untested anatomical question before treating that report as a negative inguinal study.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with strain and pubic-attachment sequences
answerChoices.rationale: This is a credible next assessment after an adequate unresolved groin ultrasound, as in B05, but the current record has not yet characterized the clinical inguinal site under provocation.

answerChoices.label: Hip MR arthrography with labral and cartilage sequences
answerChoices.rationale: A hip-joint investigation is useful for an intra-articular question. It does not correct the documented mismatch between the clinical swelling and the sampled pubic attachment.

decisionNodes.explanation: The marker, photo and timing establish that the outside report is not a completed negative dynamic inguinal assessment. Targeted groin sonography with provocation is a selected next step. Dynamic pelvic MRI remains reasonable for an adequate but unresolved study; B05 presents that different sequence. This ranking does not assert a universal ultrasound advantage over MRI or diagnose a hernia solely from the photograph.

items.value: Inferior to the inguinal ligament; medial to the common femoral vein.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The below-ligament neck medial to the vein identifies the femoral route. The trapped partial wall with absent mural signal raises concern for strangulation despite the patent remaining lumen; emergency operative exploration is appropriate rather than a manual reduction attempt.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the route correctly and applies an intervention appropriate for selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. It overweights stool passage: the reported mural perfusion raises a different concern even while the remaining lumen permits passage.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: This recognizes threatened bowel but misclassifies the neck. An indirect inguinal sac enters above the ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, rather than through the reported compartment.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This combines two plausible misreadings: assigning an inguinal route from a groin lump and treating continued intestinal passage as evidence that a reduction attempt is appropriate. Both the neck compartment and mural findings oppose that combination.

decisionNodes.explanation:
The neck below the inguinal ligament and medial to the vein identifies a femoral hernia.
A trapped portion of bowel wall can lose perfusion while the remaining lumen still permits passage: a Richter-type configuration. Suspected strangulation warrants emergency operative exploration, rather than manual reduction.
The closest error is femoral hernia with manual reduction: stool passage does not establish wall viability. Reduction can be appropriate in selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. This asks the hernia-directed intervention, not the first resuscitation order or repair technique.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; watchful waiting is unsuitable
answerChoices.rationale: The marked sac neck follows the femoral canal. Painless spontaneous reduction does not extend the selected male inguinal observation strategy to a femoral hernia; offer elective repair planning.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; watchful waiting is reasonable
answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the marked compartment but overgeneralizes the watchful-waiting evidence for selected men with inguinal hernias to femoral anatomy.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia; watchful waiting is unsuitable
answerChoices.rationale: This assigns the separate cranial defect to the marked swelling and also denies the observation option that can be reasonable for a minimally symptomatic man with a reducible inguinal hernia.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia; watchful waiting is reasonable
answerChoices.rationale: This is a reasonable classification and observation option for the separate cranial finding. It misattributes that finding to the marked lump, whose neck is in the other compartment.

decisionNodes.explanation:
The sac at the marker passes below the ligament, medial to the vein: femoral anatomy. The separate cranial defect is direct inguinal.
A painless reducing course can support watchful waiting for selected men with an inguinal hernia; femoral anatomy instead supports elective repair planning.
The nearest error identifies the femoral hernia correctly but extends the inguinal observation rule to it. This is not an emergency exploration or reduction question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which ultrasound request should be sent for {patientName}’s intermittent groin contour?

answerChoices.label: Standing strain; cine ultrasound of groin canals
answerChoices.rationale: This tests the posture and provocation associated with the separate contour while assessing hernia anatomy.

answerChoices.label: Supine strain; cine ultrasound of groin canals
answerChoices.rationale: This is a hernia protocol but repeats the posture that has not reproduced the clinical contour; standing assessment directly addresses this observed discrepancy.

answerChoices.label: Standing compression; Doppler ultrasound of groin veins
answerChoices.rationale: A posture-dependent venous swelling is a credible alternative, but the suprapubic strain-associated contour is better addressed first by dynamic canal assessment.

answerChoices.label: Supine compression; Doppler ultrasound of groin veins
answerChoices.rationale: This tests a vascular alternative in a non-reproducing posture rather than assessing the canal contour during its observed trigger.

decisionNodes.explanation: The acquisition worksheet establishes what was examined; saved-image count alone would not. Separate the attachment pain from the posture/strain-dependent contour, then request dynamic canal imaging in the reproducing position. The alternatives are actual ultrasound acquisitions rather than routine escalation to MRI. This does not make MRI inappropriate after a clinically adequate but unresolved groin assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should address {patientName}’s continuing work restriction?

answerChoices.label: Elective inguinal hernia repair referral
answerChoices.rationale: Current full-task testing supports a hernia-related work limit despite better exercise performance and completed modified shifts.

answerChoices.label: Supervised adductor strengthening rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: This can address the attachment complaint but does not account for the current load-triggered inguinal event.

answerChoices.label: Inguinal hernia surveillance with graded activity
answerChoices.rationale: This can maintain work participation, but completed modified shifts do not establish tolerance of the original stock task or address its demonstrated hernia-related restriction.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should be arranged next for {patientName}'s persistent groin symptoms?

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with strain and pubic-attachment sequences
answerChoices.rationale: The prior scan has actually assessed the clinical inguinal site under provocation. Persistent discordant symptoms and the competing musculoskeletal findings make dynamic cross-sectional assessment a selected next investigation.

answerChoices.label: Groin ultrasound with standing strain and cine loops
answerChoices.rationale: This is a credible alternative when the site or provocation was not tested. Here those elements are documented; simply repeating them does not address the remaining combined question as well.

answerChoices.label: Hip MR arthrography with labral and cartilage sequences
answerChoices.rationale: The rotation-related ache makes a hip explanation plausible, but a joint-focused examination does not answer the intermittent groin contour question alongside the attachment structures.

decisionNodes.explanation: The recorded site, positions, provocation and symptom reproduction distinguish an adequate targeted negative examination from an examination that missed the clinical question. Dynamic pelvic MRI can address persisting groin uncertainty and associated soft-tissue findings. Repeat targeted sonography remains appropriate when the site or provocation was untested; this case does not assert a universal MRI advantage or diagnose the photographed contour change by itself.

decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should be offered for {patientName}’s stock-handling limitation?

answerChoices.label: Refer for elective inguinal hernia repair
answerChoices.rationale: The limiting stock task reproduces the protrusion-associated episode. The coexisting hip changes do not establish the cause of that particular limitation.

answerChoices.label: Continue inguinal hernia surveillance with graded activity
answerChoices.rationale: This is reasonable for a minimally symptomatic inguinal hernia, but the current full-load work task is limited by the protrusion-associated event.

answerChoices.label: Refer for hip-directed physiotherapy
answerChoices.rationale: This addresses a real separate symptom, but the observed stock-lifting episode is localized to the protrusion rather than the reproduced joint-line ache.

decisionNodes.explanation: Do not let a positive radiograph select the treatment target without matching the activity that fails. Hip symptoms remain present, but the stock-handling limit accompanies the reducible inguinal finding. This is not a minimally symptomatic watchful-waiting presentation. Refer for elective repair planning while treating the joint complaint separately; no promise is made that repair will cure all groin pain.

decisionNodes.stem: Which structure forms the deficient layer in {patientName}'s described groin defect?

answerChoices.label: Transversalis fascia
answerChoices.rationale: The medial posterior-wall defect localizes to a direct inguinal hernia through weakened transversalis fascia.

answerChoices.rationale: This does not match the deficient posterior fascial layer specified for the represented direct defect.

answerChoices.label: Internal oblique muscle
answerChoices.rationale: A neighboring muscular layer is tempting, but the supplied medial posterior-wall defect points to transversalis fascia.

decisionNodes.stem: Which repair target corresponds to the protrusion marked X in {patientName}'s operative sketch?

answerChoices.label: Reinforce the transversalis fascia
answerChoices.rationale: The relationship to the vessels and ligament localizes the protrusion to a direct defect. Its deficient transversalis fascial layer is in the posterior inguinal wall.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct the deep inguinal ring
answerChoices.rationale: A cord-related indirect defect enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. That is a credible repair target for a different position of X.

answerChoices.label: Reinforce the femoral canal boundary
answerChoices.rationale: A target below the inguinal ligament would address a femoral rather than the marked inguinal protrusion.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use both orientation landmarks to localize the defect, then choose its repair target. A medial, supraligamentous protrusion is a direct posterior-wall defect involving transversalis fascia; a deep-ring target would address an indirect defect.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Following the MRI, {patientName} continues the graded exercise program with hernia observation. At review, jogging lasts longer. answerChoices.label: Hernia assessment with continued graded activity
answerChoices.rationale: Completed shifts on modified duties do not demonstrate recovery of the avoided lifting task. The current pressure/contour event supplies a hernia-related functional concern despite improved running and a coexisting attachment symptom.

answerChoices.label: Hernia observation with continued graded activity
answerChoices.rationale: This mistakes attendance on modified duties and longer jogging for unrestricted work function. It overlooks the task that remains unperformed and the observed groin event on attempting it.

answerChoices.label: Attachment reassessment with continued graded activity
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent adduction symptom is a credible reason for musculoskeletal review, but the actual remaining crate-handling interruption occurs with the separate groin pressure/contour event.

decisionNodes.explanation: Functional recovery must be read against the work actually attempted. Longer jogging and completed modified shifts do not settle the avoided lifting task. answerChoices.label: Groin ultrasound with standing strain and cine loops
answerChoices.rationale: The outside acquisition documents a different target after the event. A targeted dynamic groin assessment addresses the untested anatomical question before treating that report as a negative inguinal study.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with strain and pubic-attachment sequences
answerChoices.rationale: This is a credible next assessment after an adequate unresolved groin ultrasound, as in B05, but the current record has not yet characterized the clinical inguinal site under provocation.

answerChoices.label: Hip MR arthrography with labral and cartilage sequences
answerChoices.rationale: A hip-joint investigation is useful for an intra-articular question. It does not correct the documented mismatch between the clinical swelling and the sampled pubic attachment.

decisionNodes.explanation: The marker, photo and timing establish that the outside report is not a completed negative dynamic inguinal assessment. resultGateAfter.resultNarrative: Dynamic ultrasound shows an inguinal protrusion during strain that reduces while supine. The patient has completed an exercise trial for pubic-attachment pain and can now resist adduction with less discomfort. Lifting the relative still produces the lump and makes the patient set the relative down; the episode eases after the lump is reduced. The attachment exercise program continues.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: At a later reassessment, the patient continues a maintenance exercise program after the initial supervised phase. The groin contour withdraws when supine. During coughing it appears without pain. The caregiving log describes medial pubic pain during transfers from a low chair, including transfers when no contour is visible. A transfer from a raised chair is completed while the contour is visible. Resisted adduction reproduces the low-chair pain; hip rotation produces a different deep ache.
decisionNodes.stem: Which assessment should lead the next plan for {patientName}'s remaining caregiving difficulty?

answerChoices.label: Attachment assessment alongside the current exercise program
answerChoices.rationale: The limiting transfer pain is reproduced by adduction and occurs without the contour; a transfer can be completed with the contour present. These observations favor reviewing the attachment-related limitation rather than assigning all burden to the hernia.

answerChoices.label: Inguinal-hernia assessment alongside the current exercise program
answerChoices.rationale: The earlier hernia-associated episodes make this credible, but the later task-specific dissociation weakens attribution of the current transfer difficulty to the protrusion.

answerChoices.label: Hip-joint assessment alongside the current exercise program
answerChoices.rationale: A separate deep ache exists, but it is not the pain reproduced in the low-chair transfers. Selecting it confuses a positive examination finding with the currently limiting symptom.

decisionNodes.explanation: The current task, site and provocation matter more than the mere coexistence of a hernia. Later transfer observations dissociate the limiting medial pain from the visible contour and reproduce it with adduction. Prioritize assessment of that remaining functional problem while retaining appropriate hernia review as symptoms and preferences require.

decisionNodes.stem: Which groin-care plan best fits {patientName}'s examination and dynamic study?

answerChoices.label: Plan posterior inguinal-wall reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: The dynamic medial bulge and activity limitation support elective repair of the posterior-wall defect, rather than treating static cord fat as the symptomatic lesion.

answerChoices.label: Plan deep-ring exploration and sac repair
answerChoices.rationale: The earlier cord-fat report invites anchoring on an indirect sac, but that is not the structure changing during strain.

answerChoices.label: Plan observation with scheduled groin review
answerChoices.rationale: Observation is credible for a reducible inguinal hernia with little functional burden; recurrent interruption of work changes that balance.

decisionNodes.explanation: The changing medial posterior-wall bulge, rather than the static fat finding, identifies the symptomatic direct defect. Reducibility establishes a nonemergency setting; it does not make observation preferable when symptoms repeatedly limit work. Plan elective posterior-wall repair after normal surgical assessment. The item does not prescribe a particular mesh, approach or fixation technique.

decisionNodes.stem: Which repair target corresponds to the protrusion marked X in {patientName}'s operative sketch?

answerChoices.label: Reinforce the transversalis fascia
answerChoices.rationale: The relationship to the vessels and ligament localizes the protrusion to a direct defect. Its deficient transversalis fascial layer is in the posterior inguinal wall.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct the deep inguinal ring
answerChoices.rationale: A cord-related indirect defect enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. That is a credible repair target for a different position of X.

answerChoices.label: Reinforce the femoral canal boundary
answerChoices.rationale: A target below the inguinal ligament would address a femoral rather than the marked inguinal protrusion.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use both orientation landmarks to localize the defect, then choose its repair target. A medial, supraligamentous protrusion is a direct posterior-wall defect involving transversalis fascia; a deep-ring target would address an indirect defect.

decisionNodes.stem: Which diagnostic procedure should be selected next for {patientName}'s pain?

answerChoices.label: Dynamic inguinal and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent mechanical uncertainty after a relevant local ultrasound, together with a musculoskeletal alternative, supports selected dynamic cross-sectional evaluation rather than attributing the entire complaint to one positive maneuver.

decisionNodes.explanation: There are overlapping pain observations, not a single established cause. A technically relevant negative ultrasound reduces concern for a demonstrated hernia but leaves the deeper mechanical complaint unresolved. Selected dynamic cross-sectional assessment can address the repaired groin and competing pelvic causes. Neither the hip maneuver nor the superficial sensory response proves the cause of every symptom. This is not a routine MRI sequence for all postrepair pain, and no recurrent hernia is declared proved.

items.label: Functional course
items.value: Deep pain interrupts lifting at work. The contour change described at home is not present during this examination.

items.label: Abdominal examination

exhibit.caption: Original constructed procedure record; fictional observations

items.value: The old mesh lies directly under the external oblique and over the inguinal floor. The spermatic cord runs superficial to it. Dense scar joins the mesh edge to the cord.

answerChoices.rationale: Tests the intermittent mechanical observation rather than assuming the coexisting musculoskeletal pain explains it.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with hip and adductor assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Investigates the genuine competing musculoskeletal explanation, but is not the initial dynamic groin assessment in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic CT with abdominal-wall and groin assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Can show anatomy, but a routine cross-sectional survey does not provide the usual first dynamic assessment of an intermittent lump.

decisionNodes.explanation: The pain findings and intermittent swelling need not have the same explanation. Initial dynamic groin ultrasound can evaluate a lump that disappears at rest. Persistent uncertainty after an adequate assessment can require further investigation; MRI is not dismissed as an invalid alternative in every occult-hernia pathway.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan should be discussed with {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Elective repair consultation with operative-risk review
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates the demonstrated lesion with repeated functional limitation, while leaving the actual operation and shared decision to assessment.

answerChoices.label: Watchful waiting with an individualized symptom-triggered review
answerChoices.rationale: Applies an approach more suited to selected minimally symptomatic patients despite the supplied recurring activity limitation.

answerChoices.label: Support-garment management with an individualized scheduled review
answerChoices.rationale: Offers symptom support but treats it as the main long-term strategy despite repeated functional limitation.

A clear clinical hernia does not routinely require imaging, and a nondiagnostic study may need further assessment. The stable presentation does not require emergency treatment or a specific technique selection.

answerChoices.label: Hernia unresolved; dynamic groin ultrasound
answerChoices.rationale: The outside acquisition did not assess the reported intermittent groin event. It cannot exclude a hernia; a properly targeted dynamic study is an appropriate completion plan.

answerChoices.label: Hernia excluded; hip-directed rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The hip findings can explain part of the pain, but do not make the mistargeted or resting negative study an exclusion of the photographed swelling.

answerChoices.label: Hernia established; elective inguinal repair planning
answerChoices.rationale: The photographed swelling and limited outside study do not establish the anatomic diagnosis needed to commit to a repair pathway.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial care plan best fits {patientName}'s activity-limiting symptoms?

answerChoices.label: Abdominal-attachment rehabilitation; hernia observation
answerChoices.rationale: The limiting complaint follows trunk loading and the attachment finding; the minimally symptomatic reducible hernia need not be repaired to begin that care.

answerChoices.label: Adductor-focused rehabilitation with initial hernia observation
answerChoices.rationale: This also avoids premature repair, but targets an attachment not supported by the reproduced symptom or MRI location.

answerChoices.label: Elective hernia repair before abdominal rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the coexisting protrusion as the first intervention despite discordance with the limiting symptom pattern.

decisionNodes.explanation: Weigh functional burden and the reproduced movement pattern, not only the positive groin image. The limiting pain tracks the lower abdominal attachment during trunk loading; the reducible inguinal finding has little functional burden. Targeted rehabilitation with initial hernia observation is a defensible first plan. This does not establish a guarantee about future pain or hernia behavior.

Passive hip rotation does not reproduce that pain.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: After the MRI, {patientName} begins a graded exercise program with hernia observation. At review, walking has progressed to sustained jogging. The groin contour still appears with coughing and withdraws on lying down, as before. Work shifts are completed without interruption. MRI review still shows the small protrusion and the attachment signal change.
decisionNodes.stem: Which care adjustment is best supported by {patientName}'s interval course?

answerChoices.label: Continue observation while advancing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: Function improves without changing the hernia finding. The interval response supports the current conservative approach rather than using persistent imaging alone as an indication to alter the plan.

answerChoices.label: Start repair planning while advancing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: A persistent protrusion can attract repair planning, but the actual functional trajectory does not establish a new hernia-related limitation that explains a need to change this initial plan.

answerChoices.label: Start repair planning before advancing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: This gives an unchanged imaging finding priority over the improving function and pauses a program that is helping. It assumes the hernia must be corrected before activity can progress.

decisionNodes.explanation: The MRI finding has not changed while function has improved during the exercise program. That response supports continuing rehabilitation and observation of the reducible, minimally limiting hernia in this man, with counseling and reassessment if symptoms change. It does not show that elective repair is forbidden or that imaging alone proves the source of all pain.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should be arranged next for {patientName}'s intermittent groin swelling?

answerChoices.label: Groin ultrasound with standing strain and cine loops
answerChoices.rationale: The outside acquisition documents a different target after the event. A targeted dynamic groin assessment addresses the untested anatomical question before treating that report as a negative inguinal study.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with strain and pubic-attachment sequences
answerChoices.rationale: This is a credible next assessment after an adequate unresolved groin ultrasound, as in B05, but the current record has not yet characterized the clinical inguinal site under provocation.

answerChoices.label: Hip MR arthrography with labral and cartilage sequences
answerChoices.rationale: A hip-joint investigation is useful for an intra-articular question. It does not correct the documented mismatch between the clinical swelling and the sampled pubic attachment.

decisionNodes.explanation: The marker, photo and timing establish that the outside report is not a completed negative dynamic inguinal assessment. Targeted groin sonography with provocation is a selected next step. Dynamic pelvic MRI remains reasonable for an adequate but unresolved study; B05 presents that different sequence. This ranking does not assert a universal ultrasound advantage over MRI or diagnose a hernia solely from the photograph.

decisionNodes.stem: When should {patientName}'s hernia referral be arranged?

answerChoices.label: Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after rehabilitation is completed
answerChoices.rationale: Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
answerChoices.rationale: Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.

decisionNodes.explanation: The improvement on resisted adduction does not explain away the persisting interruption of caregiving during a reducible-lump episode. Elective hernia assessment can proceed while attachment rehabilitation continues. Neither completion of every exercise goal nor anatomical growth is a prerequisite to assessment of an already function-limiting hernia.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI with strain and pubic-attachment sequences
answerChoices.rationale: The prior scan has actually assessed the clinical inguinal site under provocation. Persistent discordant symptoms and the competing musculoskeletal findings make dynamic cross-sectional assessment a selected next investigation.

answerChoices.label: Groin ultrasound with standing strain and cine loops
answerChoices.rationale: This is a credible alternative when the site or provocation was not tested. Here those elements are documented; simply repeating them does not address the remaining combined question as well.

question.stem: Which hernia type and hernia-directed intervention fit these findings in {patientName}?

exhibit.caption: Targeted groin ultrasound

items.label: Sac neck
items.value: Inferior to the inguinal ligament; medial to the common femoral vein.

items.label: Bowel at the neck
items.value: Part of one bowel wall protrudes through the opening. The remaining lumen stays within the abdomen.

items.label: Compression
items.value: The protruding wall remains at the opening.

items.label: Doppler
items.value: No mural signal in the protruding wall. Adjacent bowel has mural signal at the same settings.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The below-ligament neck medial to the vein identifies the femoral route. The trapped partial wall with absent mural signal raises concern for strangulation despite the patent remaining lumen; emergency operative exploration is appropriate rather than a manual reduction attempt.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the route correctly and applies an intervention appropriate for selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. It overweights stool passage: the reported mural perfusion raises a different concern even while the remaining lumen permits passage.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This identifies the route correctly and applies an intervention appropriate for selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. It overweights stool passage: the reported mural perfusion raises a different concern even while the remaining lumen permits passage.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: This recognizes threatened bowel but misclassifies the neck. An indirect inguinal sac enters above the ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, rather than through the reported compartment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This recognizes threatened bowel but misclassifies the neck. An indirect inguinal sac enters above the ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, rather than through the reported compartment.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This combines two plausible misreadings: assigning an inguinal route from a groin lump and treating continued intestinal passage as evidence that a reduction attempt is appropriate. Both the neck compartment and mural findings oppose that combination.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This combines two plausible misreadings: assigning an inguinal route from a groin lump and treating continued intestinal passage as evidence that a reduction attempt is appropriate. Both the neck compartment and mural findings oppose that combination.

question.explanation:
The neck below the inguinal ligament and medial to the vein identifies a femoral hernia.
A trapped portion of bowel wall can lose perfusion while the remaining lumen still permits passage: a Richter-type configuration. Suspected strangulation warrants emergency operative exploration, rather than manual reduction.
The closest error is femoral hernia with manual reduction: stool passage does not establish wall viability. Reduction can be appropriate in selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. This asks the hernia-directed intervention, not the first resuscitation order or repair technique.

question.stem: Which hernia type and hernia-directed intervention fit these findings in {patientName}?

exhibit.caption: Targeted groin ultrasound

items.label: Sac neck
items.value: Inferior to the inguinal ligament; medial to the common femoral vein.

items.label: Bowel at the neck
items.value: Part of one bowel wall protrudes through the opening. The remaining lumen stays within the abdomen.

items.label: Compression
items.value: The protruding wall remains at the opening.

items.label: Doppler
items.value: No mural signal in the protruding wall. Adjacent bowel has mural signal at the same settings.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The below-ligament neck medial to the vein identifies the femoral route. The trapped partial wall with absent mural signal raises concern for strangulation despite the patent remaining lumen; emergency operative exploration is appropriate rather than a manual reduction attempt.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the route correctly and applies an intervention appropriate for selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. It overweights stool passage: the reported mural perfusion raises a different concern even while the remaining lumen permits passage.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This identifies the route correctly and applies an intervention appropriate for selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. It overweights stool passage: the reported mural perfusion raises a different concern even while the remaining lumen permits passage.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: This recognizes threatened bowel but misclassifies the neck. An indirect inguinal sac enters above the ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, rather than through the reported compartment.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This recognizes threatened bowel but misclassifies the neck. An indirect inguinal sac enters above the ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, rather than through the reported compartment.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This combines two plausible misreadings: assigning an inguinal route from a groin lump and treating continued intestinal passage as evidence that a reduction attempt is appropriate. Both the neck compartment and mural findings oppose that combination.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This combines two plausible misreadings: assigning an inguinal route from a groin lump and treating continued intestinal passage as evidence that a reduction attempt is appropriate. Both the neck compartment and mural findings oppose that combination.

question.explanation:
The neck below the inguinal ligament and medial to the vein identifies a femoral hernia.
A trapped portion of bowel wall can lose perfusion while the remaining lumen still permits passage: a Richter-type configuration. Suspected strangulation warrants emergency operative exploration, rather than manual reduction.
The closest error is femoral hernia with manual reduction: stool passage does not establish wall viability. Reduction can be appropriate in selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. This asks the hernia-directed intervention, not the first resuscitation order or repair technique.

answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the marked compartment but overgeneralizes the watchful-waiting evidence for selected men with inguinal hernias to femoral anatomy.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: This assigns the separate cranial defect to the marked swelling and also denies the observation option that can be reasonable for a minimally symptomatic man with a reducible inguinal hernia.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia; watchful waiting is reasonable

node.stem: Which type of hernia do the ultrasound findings identify in {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia
answerChoices.rationale: The neck lies below the inguinal ligament and medial to the common femoral vein, identifying the femoral-canal route.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Direct inguinal anatomy is defined at Hesselbach's triangle medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. The recorded neck instead follows the below-ligament compartment beside the common femoral vein.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An indirect inguinal sac enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. The reported below-ligament neck and venous relationship identify a different route.

node.explanation: The sac neck's relationship to the ligament and vein identifies a femoral hernia. Direct and indirect inguinal labels refer to different anatomical routes.

node.currentUpdate: Ultrasound classification: femoral hernia. {patientName} now completes his usual caregiving lifts. The groin bulge disappears when he lies down. The groin is nontender, the abdomen is soft and not distended, and he reports no vomiting.
node.stem: Which plan should be offered for {patientName}'s groin hernia at this visit?

answerChoices.label: Plan elective hernia repair
answerChoices.rationale: The established femoral anatomy supports timely elective repair despite improved function. The reducing, nontender presentation without obstructive features does not establish an emergency.

answerChoices.label: Plan scheduled hernia surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: Observation can be appropriate for selected minimally symptomatic inguinal hernias in men. Improvement in lifting does not extend that observation rule to the identified femoral route.

answerChoices.label: Plan emergency hernia exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The femoral type warrants repair planning, but the current record does not show the persistent painful irreducible or obstructed presentation needed to favor emergency exploration here.

node.explanation: Combine the established type with the current acuity. A stable reducing femoral hernia warrants timely elective repair planning even when symptoms have improved. The inguinal watchful-waiting rule for selected men does not apply to this anatomy. New pain, irreducibility or obstructive/ischemic concern would change the urgency; no fixed deadline or repair technique is specified.

node.currentUpdate: After the MRI-result visit, {patientName} continues rehabilitation with hernia observation. At a later review, repeated trunk flexion is completed and no longer reproduces the original suprapubic pain. The work log now records pauses with a superficial ache at the inguinal fold during coughing and crate lifting. In the clinic the familiar superficial ache occurs while the groin contour is visible; the contour withdraws when supine. Hip rotation still produces a deeper ache that the patient distinguishes from the work episodes.
node.stem: Which change should be made to {patientName}'s current care plan?

answerChoices.label: Prioritize hernia assessment while continuing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The earlier painless protrusion is not proof that all later episodes are incidental. A different, now limiting groin symptom tracks the protrusion after the original flexion-provoked complaint improves.

answerChoices.label: Prioritize attachment reassessment while continuing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: This carries forward the earlier MRI-associated pain assignment despite resolution of its reproduced functional problem and a different current site/provocation.

answerChoices.label: Prioritize hip-joint assessment while continuing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: A hip-related ache remains, but the patient and observed task distinguish it from the superficial symptom stopping work.

node.explanation: Attribution can change over time. The original flexion-provoked suprapubic limitation has improved, whereas a different current superficial symptom occurs with the protrusion and interrupts work. That supports elective hernia assessment without assuming that repair will treat every groin ache or stopping care for coexisting symptoms.

node.stem: Which focused groin ultrasound acquisition should trace {patientName}’s recorded tissue course proximally?

answerChoices.label: Deep inguinal ring during Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: The lateral-to-epigastric cord course points toward the deep ring. Following the moving tissue proximally there can establish whether it enters through a defect rather than infer the diagnosis from a distal contour or an adductor study.

answerChoices.label: Posterior inguinal wall during Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: This is the nearby direct-hernia region, medial to the epigastric vessels. It does not best follow the lateral cord course actually recorded.

answerChoices.label: Femoral canal during Valsalva
answerChoices.rationale: This is another clinically important groin region, below the ligament and medial to the femoral vein; it does not trace the recorded tissue along the inguinal cord.

node.explanation: Use the anatomical course to choose the additional focus. The deep ring is lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels; the direct region lies medially and the femoral canal follows a different route below the ligament. The recorded distal fat movement is not itself proof of a proximal hernia neck. Follow its origin dynamically rather than infer that the tendon examination settled the contour question. A full study can include all regions and positions; this asks for the added focus, not a universally sufficient protocol.

node.stem: Which repair should be discussed for {patientName}’s recurrent groin defect?

answerChoices.label: Totally extraperitoneal repair
answerChoices.rationale: The old report describes an anterior mesh plane. A posterior preperitoneal approach is the offered route that avoids re-entering that operated plane for a symptomatic recurrence.

answerChoices.label: Anterior Lichtenstein mesh repair
answerChoices.rationale: This is a valid primary repair, but repeating the anterior mesh approach re-enters the prior operative plane in this recurrence.

answerChoices.label: Anterior Shouldice tissue repair
answerChoices.rationale: Changing to a tissue repair does not change the fact that this is another anterior-plane operation after the recorded anterior mesh repair.

node.explanation: The current functional episode remains consistent with the demonstrated hernia rather than being dismissed because hip disease also exists. The new decision concerns recurrence. Mesh fixed in the inguinal floor and covered by external oblique indicates a previous anterior repair; the offered posterior preperitoneal repair uses the other plane. This does not establish TEP as superior to every other posterior approach or promise that hernia repair cures the separate hip ache.

exhibit.caption: Targeted groin ultrasound: constructed findings

items.label: At the skin marker
items.value: A bowel-containing sac has its neck below the inguinal ligament, medial to the common femoral vein. It empties when supine.

items.label: Separate cranial finding
items.value: Fat protrudes through a defect above the inguinal ligament, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; watchful waiting is unsuitable
answerChoices.rationale: The marked sac neck follows the femoral canal. Painless spontaneous reduction does not extend the selected male inguinal observation strategy to a femoral hernia; offer elective repair planning.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; watchful waiting is reasonable
answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the marked compartment but overgeneralizes the watchful-waiting evidence for selected men with inguinal hernias to femoral anatomy.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia; watchful waiting is unsuitable
answerChoices.rationale: This assigns the separate cranial defect to the marked swelling and also denies the observation option that can be reasonable for a minimally symptomatic man with a reducible inguinal hernia.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia; watchful waiting is reasonable
answerChoices.rationale: This is a reasonable classification and observation option for the separate cranial finding. It misattributes that finding to the marked lump, whose neck is in the other compartment.

node.explanation:
The sac at the marker passes below the ligament, medial to the vein: femoral anatomy. The separate cranial defect is direct inguinal.
A painless reducing course can support watchful waiting for selected men with an inguinal hernia; femoral anatomy instead supports elective repair planning.

exhibit.caption: Targeted groin ultrasound

items.label: Sac neck
items.value: Inferior to the inguinal ligament; medial to the common femoral vein.

items.label: Bowel at the neck
items.value: Part of one bowel wall protrudes through the opening. The remaining lumen stays within the abdomen.

items.label: Compression
items.value: The protruding wall remains at the opening.

items.label: Doppler
items.value: No mural signal in the protruding wall. Adjacent bowel has mural signal at the same settings.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The below-ligament neck medial to the vein identifies the femoral route. The trapped partial wall with absent mural signal raises concern for strangulation despite the patent remaining lumen; emergency operative exploration is appropriate rather than a manual reduction attempt.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This identifies the route correctly and applies an intervention appropriate for selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. It overweights stool passage: the reported mural perfusion raises a different concern even while the remaining lumen permits passage.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; operative exploration
answerChoices.rationale: This recognizes threatened bowel but misclassifies the neck. An indirect inguinal sac enters above the ligament, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, rather than through the reported compartment.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia; manual reduction
answerChoices.rationale: This combines two plausible misreadings: assigning an inguinal route from a groin lump and treating continued intestinal passage as evidence that a reduction attempt is appropriate. Both the neck compartment and mural findings oppose that combination.

node.explanation:
The neck below the inguinal ligament and medial to the vein identifies a femoral hernia.
A trapped portion of bowel wall can lose perfusion while the remaining lumen still permits passage: a Richter-type configuration. Suspected strangulation warrants emergency operative exploration, rather than manual reduction.
The closest error is femoral hernia with manual reduction: stool passage does not establish wall viability. Reduction can be appropriate in selected acute nonreducing hernias without suspected strangulation. This asks the hernia-directed intervention, not the first resuscitation order or repair technique.

answerChoices.label: Femoral hernia
answerChoices.rationale: The neck lies below the inguinal ligament and medial to the common femoral vein, identifying the femoral-canal route.

answerChoices.label: Direct inguinal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: Direct inguinal anatomy is defined at Hesselbach's triangle medial to the inferior epigastric vessels. The recorded neck instead follows the below-ligament compartment beside the common femoral vein.

answerChoices.label: Indirect inguinal hernia
answerChoices.rationale: An indirect inguinal sac enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. The reported below-ligament neck and venous relationship identify a different route.

priorNodes.explanation: The sac neck's relationship to the ligament and vein identifies a femoral hernia. Direct and indirect inguinal labels refer to different anatomical routes.

answerChoices.label: Plan elective hernia repair
answerChoices.rationale: The established femoral anatomy supports timely elective repair despite improved function. The reducing, nontender presentation without obstructive features does not establish an emergency.

answerChoices.label: Plan scheduled hernia surveillance

answerChoices.label: Plan emergency hernia exploration
answerChoices.rationale: The femoral type warrants repair planning, but the current record does not show the persistent painful irreducible or obstructed presentation needed to favor emergency exploration here.

node.stem: When should {patientName}'s hernia referral be arranged?

answerChoices.label: Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after rehabilitation is completed
answerChoices.rationale: Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
answerChoices.rationale: Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.

node.explanation: The improvement on resisted adduction does not explain away the persisting interruption of caregiving during a reducible-lump episode. Elective hernia assessment can proceed while attachment rehabilitation continues. Neither completion of every exercise goal nor anatomical growth is a prerequisite to assessment of an already function-limiting hernia.

resultGateAfter.resultNarrative: Dynamic ultrasound shows an inguinal protrusion during strain that reduces while supine. The patient has completed an exercise trial for pubic-attachment pain and can now resist adduction with less discomfort. Lifting the relative still produces the lump and makes the patient set the relative down; the episode eases after the lump is reduced. The attachment exercise program continues.

node.currentUpdate: At a later reassessment, the patient continues a maintenance exercise program after the initial supervised phase. The groin contour withdraws when supine. During coughing it appears without pain. The caregiving log describes medial pubic pain during transfers from a low chair, including transfers when no contour is visible. A transfer from a raised chair is completed while the contour is visible. Resisted adduction reproduces the low-chair pain; hip rotation produces a different deep ache.
node.stem: Which assessment should lead the next plan for {patientName}'s remaining caregiving difficulty?

answerChoices.label: Attachment assessment alongside the current exercise program
answerChoices.rationale: The limiting transfer pain is reproduced by adduction and occurs without the contour; a transfer can be completed with the contour present. These observations favor reviewing the attachment-related limitation rather than assigning all burden to the hernia.

answerChoices.label: Inguinal-hernia assessment alongside the current exercise program
answerChoices.rationale: The earlier hernia-associated episodes make this credible, but the later task-specific dissociation weakens attribution of the current transfer difficulty to the protrusion.

answerChoices.label: Hip-joint assessment alongside the current exercise program
answerChoices.rationale: A separate deep ache exists, but it is not the pain reproduced in the low-chair transfers. Selecting it confuses a positive examination finding with the currently limiting symptom.

node.explanation: The current task, site and provocation matter more than the mere coexistence of a hernia. Prioritize assessment of that remaining functional problem while retaining appropriate hernia review as symptoms and preferences require.

node.stem: When should {patientName}'s hernia referral be arranged?

answerChoices.label: Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after rehabilitation is completed
answerChoices.rationale: Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
answerChoices.rationale: Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.

node.explanation: The earlier minimally limiting protrusion was observed while the attachment problem was treated. answerChoices.label: Standing groin ultrasound during straining
answerChoices.rationale: Targets the intermittent protrusion at the initial imaging stage.

answerChoices.label: Dynamic groin MRI during straining
answerChoices.rationale: Is a credible problem-solving option, rather than a hip-only protocol deliberately prevented from assessing the reported protrusion.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic CT with multiplanar groin assessment

priorNodes.explanation: The pain findings and intermittent swelling need not have the same explanation. Initial dynamic groin ultrasound can evaluate a lump that disappears at rest. answerChoices.label: Hernia unresolved; dynamic groin ultrasound
answerChoices.rationale: The outside acquisition did not assess the reported intermittent groin event. It cannot exclude a hernia; a properly targeted dynamic study is an appropriate completion plan.

answerChoices.label: Hernia excluded; hip-directed rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The hip findings can explain part of the pain, but do not make the mistargeted or resting negative study an exclusion of the photographed swelling.

answerChoices.label: Hernia established; elective inguinal repair planning
answerChoices.rationale: The photographed swelling and limited outside study do not establish the anatomic diagnosis needed to commit to a repair pathway.

priorNodes.explanation: Interpret an ultrasound result together with its actual target and acquisition. Choose the protocol that resolves the particular unanswered diagnostic question.

node.stem: Which management discussion should follow {patientName}'s returned imaging and examination findings?

answerChoices.label: Discuss hernia repair and hip-pain assessment

answerChoices.label: Trial hip rehabilitation with hernia observation

answerChoices.label: Discuss elective hernia repair without hip assessment

Neither path promises resolution of a separate musculoskeletal problem.

answerChoices.label: Standing dynamic ultrasound of the groin
answerChoices.rationale: A targeted dynamic study tests the intermittent groin event rather than treating a resting or differently targeted examination as exclusion.

answerChoices.label: Routine supine MRI of the groin and hip
answerChoices.rationale: Hip pathology is a competing explanation, but this routine joint protocol does not first characterize the intermittent groin event.

answerChoices.label: Contrast CT of the groin and pelvis at rest

priorNodes.explanation: A negative resting view does not necessarily test an intermittent strain-related protrusion. This does not assert that dynamic MRI is inferior after an adequate unresolved ultrasound.

node.stem: Which next plan best addresses {patientName}'s remaining activity limitation?

answerChoices.label: Elective hernia consultation with ongoing musculoskeletal care
answerChoices.rationale: Activity-limiting bulge-associated episodes persist despite improvement of the musculoskeletal symptoms; discuss the symptomatic hernia without promising relief of every groin symptom.

answerChoices.label: Further musculoskeletal rehabilitation before hernia consultation
answerChoices.rationale: This prioritizes the improving musculoskeletal component while leaving the persistent activity-limiting bulge-related episodes unaddressed.

answerChoices.label: Pelvic MRI before hernia or rehabilitation planning
answerChoices.rationale: Further imaging may help unresolved pain, but the dynamic anatomic finding and reproducible functional burden already support a hernia consultation.

node.explanation: Use the response trajectory as well as the scan. The hip-related ache has improved, but the reproducible bulge-associated interruption remains. Consultation is not a compulsory operation and does not promise that repair cures rotation-related pain.

node.stem: When should {patientName}'s hernia referral be arranged?

answerChoices.label: Refer during ongoing rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: The remaining functional interruption tracks the reducible protrusion despite improvement in the coexisting attachment/joint symptoms. Elective assessment need not await completion of that treatment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after rehabilitation is completed
answerChoices.rationale: Residual musculoskeletal symptoms can coexist with a hernia that already limits function. Treating them first as an absolute referral prerequisite delays the separately supported hernia assessment.

answerChoices.label: Refer after repeat imaging documents progression
answerChoices.rationale: Anatomical enlargement is not required before discussing an already demonstrated activity-limiting inguinal hernia. This mistakes imaging change for the relevant functional criterion.

node.explanation: The exercise response improves one symptom source without resolving the separate lifting interruption associated with the reducible protrusion. Elective hernia assessment can proceed during the ongoing rehabilitation. Neither disappearance of every musculoskeletal symptom nor imaging enlargement is required before assessment of a function-limiting hernia. Referral is not a commitment to an operation or a particular technique.

node.stem: Which assessment should lead the plan for the activity that still limits {patientName}'s work?

answerChoices.label: Hip-focused musculoskeletal assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The limiting low-shelf task and reproduced deep ache now track hip movement while the visible protrusion is tolerated. Prior hernia-related episodes do not establish the cause of this different remaining limitation.

answerChoices.label: Hernia-focused surgical assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The demonstrated hernia and earlier lifting episodes make this credible, but the later functional record does not connect the remaining low-shelf limitation to current protrusion episodes.

answerChoices.label: Pubic-attachment rehabilitation assessment

node.explanation: A demonstrated hernia need not explain every later groin complaint. Prioritize assessment of that remaining limitation; the hernia can still be discussed according to symptoms, risk and preference.

node.currentUpdate: At review the deep ache on hip rotation has subsided. During stock lifting, a superficial groin lump still makes {patientName} stop; the episode settles when the lump is pressed back. Standing cough reproduces the lump on examination. Lying supine makes it withdraw.
node.stem: Which next plan should be offered for {patientName}’s remaining work limitation?

answerChoices.label: Offer elective inguinal hernia repair
answerChoices.rationale: The demonstrated reducible protrusion now tracks the task-limiting episodes while the separate hip ache has improved. Elective repair planning addresses the remaining limitation.

answerChoices.label: Repeat a course of hip rehabilitation
answerChoices.rationale: This would be reasonable for continuing hip-limited function, but the recorded residual limitation now follows the protrusion rather than the improved rotation ache.

answerChoices.label: Repeat targeted dynamic groin ultrasonography
answerChoices.rationale: Another diagnostic study is not the needed step when the protrusion has already been demonstrated and is reproduced clinically during the limiting activity.

node.explanation: Use the interval response to separate the two complaints. This does not guarantee that repair will treat unrelated musculoskeletal pain.

node.stem: Which repair target corresponds to the protrusion marked X in {patientName}'s operative sketch?

answerChoices.label: Reinforce the transversalis fascia
answerChoices.rationale: The relationship to the vessels and ligament localizes the protrusion to a direct defect. Its deficient transversalis fascial layer is in the posterior inguinal wall.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct the deep inguinal ring
answerChoices.rationale: A cord-related indirect defect enters the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels. That is a credible repair target for a different position of X.

answerChoices.label: Reinforce the femoral canal boundary
answerChoices.rationale: A target below the inguinal ligament would address a femoral rather than the marked inguinal protrusion.

node.explanation: Use both orientation landmarks to localize the defect, then choose its repair target. A medial, supraligamentous protrusion is a direct posterior-wall defect involving transversalis fascia; a deep-ring target would address an indirect defect.

visibleContext.presentation: {patientName}, a 63-year-old man, returns to clinic for a right-groin bulge that interrupts his delivery work. An earlier supine scan described fat beside the cord. On standing examination the bulge appears with coughing and reduces when he lies down; his abdomen is soft and he is eating normally.

profiles.presentation: {patientName}, a 63-year-old man, returns to clinic for a right-groin bulge that interrupts his delivery work. An earlier supine scan described fat beside the cord. On standing examination the bulge appears with coughing and reduces when he lies down; his abdomen is soft and he is eating normally.

node.stem: Which groin-care plan best fits {patientName}'s examination and dynamic study?

answerChoices.label: Plan posterior inguinal-wall reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: The dynamic medial bulge and activity limitation support elective repair of the posterior-wall defect, rather than treating static cord fat as the symptomatic lesion.

answerChoices.label: Plan deep-ring exploration and sac repair
answerChoices.rationale: The earlier cord-fat report invites anchoring on an indirect sac, but that is not the structure changing during strain.

answerChoices.label: Plan observation with scheduled groin review
answerChoices.rationale: Observation is credible for a reducible inguinal hernia with little functional burden; recurrent interruption of work changes that balance.

node.explanation: The changing medial posterior-wall bulge, rather than the static fat finding, identifies the symptomatic direct defect. Reducibility establishes a nonemergency setting; it does not make observation preferable when symptoms repeatedly limit work. Plan elective posterior-wall repair after normal surgical assessment. The item does not prescribe a particular mesh, approach or fixation technique.

items.label: Cord region
items.value: Fat beside the cord remains unchanged during strain; no moving sac follows the cord

items.label: Below the ligament
items.value: No protrusion appears during the same maneuvers

node.stem: Which investigation should {patientName} undergo next?

answerChoices.label: Dynamic pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent uncertainty after an adequately targeted study and a competing musculoskeletal explanation support dynamic cross-sectional assessment rather than assuming the earlier nerve response classified every symptom.

answerChoices.label: Repeat ilioinguinal diagnostic nerve block
answerChoices.rationale: A prior response concerning the superficial burning does not establish the cause of the remaining deep mechanical symptoms.

node.explanation: The earlier block informed one pain component, not every later symptom. The current examination and adequately targeted dynamic ultrasound leave uncertainty, with a plausible musculoskeletal contributor. Dynamic cross-sectional imaging can address that unresolved question. This is not a universal MRI-before-ultrasound hierarchy, nor proof that the intermittent contour change is a recurrent hernia.
